rubric.exceeds: Every step, value, or rendered choice is accurate and faithful to the stated criteria, with no notable errors.
rubric.meets: The work is accurate and faithful to the stated criteria, with at most one minor self-correctable error.
rubric.developing: The work is mostly accurate but has one or more errors that change the result or the intended effect.
rubric.beginning: Multiple accuracy or fidelity errors prevent the work from meeting the stated criteria.

rubric.exceeds: Every claim or choice is backed by specific evidence or clearly explained reasoning a reader can follow unaided.
rubric.meets: Most claims or choices are backed by evidence or reasoning, with only small gaps.
rubric.developing: Some claims are supported but several are asserted without support.
rubric.beginning: Claims are asserted with little or no supporting evidence or reasoning.

rubric.exceeds: The record shows the actual working order, including abandoned attempts and dead ends, in enough detail to reconstruct the session.
rubric.meets: The required log, trace, or notes are present and record what was done and why.

scoring_judgment_guidance: Score this session with the rubric below, not against a fixed answer key — a creative or analytical task legitimately has more than one valid solution. Score only what a first concept model on sustained making or composing can show: a wrong prediction or a rough first attempt is expected here and must not reduce the score, provided the record is complete and honest. Record the level reached on each dimension with one specific reason drawn from the actual submission. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task on sustained making or composing.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name a next step.
formative_check: Explain the modelled approach to sustained making or composing in your own words and name the step most likely to go wrong.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.
mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use sketch or rehearsal record, created or performed work, artist statement, critique response, revision log, and portfolio reflection; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.

mastery_interpretation.secure: At least 85% with accurate independent application and adequate evidence and reasoning.
mastery_interpretation.developing: 70–84% or inconsistent explanation; assign targeted review and a fresh transfer check.
mastery_interpretation.not_yet: Below 70% or a missing prerequisite; reteach the smallest gap and reassess with new evidence.
mastery_interpretation.rule: A unit score is one evidence source, not the sole basis for long-term mastery.

unit_assessment_reference.note: This lesson is one session inside the unit; the unit assessment record above is the summative instrument, and this lesson rubric scores only this session's evidence.

remediation_plan: Reteaching for sustained making or composing follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for sustained making or composing, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to sustained making or composing works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of sustained making or composing, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking sustained making or composing mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension_plan: Apply sustained making or composing under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on sustained making or composing rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
accommodation_note: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries exactly the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording. A written or notated account of the intended performance is a full substitute.

Any model, source, or artifact under study is supplied in an accessible parallel form: text alternative or transcript, described version, and a tactile or enlarged rendering where the original is visual. The learner is never required to perceive the source in one specific channel to analyse it.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
